subject: Intro: MAP & evaluation timeline for Novamed pilot
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@novamed.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro: MAP & evaluation timeline for Novamed pilot

Hi Lena —

Great talking with you last week. Per our conversation, I wanted to kick off the mutual action plan (MAP) for the Novamed pilot so we have clear goals, owners, and a closing timeline. I attached a short MAP template to make it easy to fill in.

High-level goals (please confirm):
- Pilot objective: reduce manual triage time by 40% using Redwood inference for clinical note summarization
- Success metric: end-to-end latency < 350ms at 95th percentile and > 80% accuracy on our eval set
- Timeline target: pilot sign-off and procurement by the end of Q2

Proposed near-term milestones:
1) MAP completion & stakeholder roster (this week)
2) 1-hour technical onboarding + environment access (wk of Apr 18)
3) Full eval runs + quality review (2–3 weeks)
4) Procurement/contracting (final week before sign-off)

Ask: Can you confirm the goals above and the right internal contacts (who should own security sign-off, procurement, and clinical validation)? Also please confirm whether a one-week shift to the pilot start is acceptable (we can be flexible).

I’ve copied Monica (customer success) and Tessa (solutions engineer) to help with the technical plan.

Attachment: Novamed-MAP-template.xlsx (Excel, 42KB)

Thanks — looking forward to getting this on paper and moving fast.

— Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks, Diego — this looks good and aligned with internal priorities. Quick notes:
- Confirmed champion: Lena Ortiz (Clinical Ops) — I will own clinical validation and stakeholder coordination.
- Procurement lead: Sabrina Cho (cc’d) — she’ll handle commercial approvals and PO timing.
- Security/IT: I’ll loop in our InfoSec lead after we confirm the MAP content.

Timeline: we’d prefer to push the technical onboarding one week later (wk of Apr 25) because of internal calendar constraints — the rest of the schedule can slide accordingly. Targeting sign-off by the end of June still works for us.

Next step: can you propose 2–3 times for a 60-minute kickoff and share the MAP file back with the stakeholder columns filled in where you already have owners?

Thanks Lena — that works. I’ve updated the MAP template with the owner columns populated for the items we discussed (attached). Highlights of the updated plan:
- Technical onboarding: propose Apr 26 10:00–11:00 PT or Apr 27 13:00–14:00 PT (please pick one)
- Deliverables before onboarding: sample data spec, test account + SSO link, and access to a small validation set
- Evaluation cadence: weekly quality syncs during the 2-week eval run; Monica will track quality regressions and baseline metrics
- Contracting: Sabrina, we’ll surface an initial SOW and estimate after the eval (I’ll share a short draft and the HubSpot deal after kickoff)

Attachment: Novamed-MAP-template.xlsx (updated)
Shared links: https://hubspot.example.com/deals/ND-11523 | https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-Novamed-MAP

If you confirm Apr 26 or Apr 27 I’ll send a calendar invite and include the meeting agenda.

Thanks — Diego

Internal notes — please treat as internal-only prep ahead of the kickoff:

Monica — can you prepare a short slide (3 bullets) on success criteria collection and the weekly quality tracker we’ll use? I want a single dashboard we can share with Lena each week.

Tessa — we’ll need an environment checklist: sample size for the eval, expected seq lengths, tokenization notes, and any preferred quantization profile. Also please prepare a short list of what we need from Novamed for the SSO + test account.

I’ll draft the kickoff agenda and send invites once Lena confirms Apr 26/27. Also flagging that procurement typically needs a 2-week lead for PO sign-off — Sabrina is already on the thread.

— Diego
